script.base: A modest 42.5 total and a 5.5-point home favorite point to a control game, not a shootout. New England leads by halftime or late, leans on the run against a Carolina front that has allowed 5.64 YPC and 10 runs of 10-plus, and protects a lead with Stevenson/Henderson/Maye carries. Carolina (implied 18.5) trails and has to throw with Bryce Young, who is at -0.40 EPA/dropback when blitzed.
script.flip1: Carolina hangs around or leads, so Hubbard (if active) keeps a 14-carry workload and the rush under dies, while Maye is forced off the run game and Stevenson never gets the late clock-killing carries.
script.flip2: New England is up big early: Carolina abandons the run (Hubbard under cashes, but a late scratch or a committee benching can also void or cap Stevenson), and NE starter snaps get trimmed. Unsaved wind/rain could also drag both offenses into a slog.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report only; final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack. CAR: Xavier Legette Out (hamstring; 15 targets, 8 yards) and Ja'Tavion Sanders Out (ankle; 14 targets, 92 yards) vacate about 10 targets a game toward McMillan (Q, calf), Renfrow, Tremayne, Tremble and Hubbard's checkdowns. Hubbard Questionable (calf) is the rush-volume pivot: if he sits, Dowdle (19/51) is next man, but he is Q not Out so this is a watch, not a confirmed sleeper. Wonnum Out (hip) and Patrick Jones II Out (hamstring) remove two Panthers linebackers, which helps NE TE/RB throws and the run. NE: Jared Wilson Out (ankle) and Mike Onwenu Questionable (shoulder) are guard losses, so rushing efficiency should be down and quick throws to RB/TE up, with deep WR yards down. Gonzalez Questionable (hamstring) is a CAR pass-game swing only if he sits. Chaisson Questionable (knee). Sources: pack injury report and weeks 1-3 target/carry counts.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack; shell is unknown. Location splits stand in: NE allows 9.1 YPA left (41), 11.29 middle (17), 8.37 right (30). CAR allows 5.49 left (39), 10.33 middle (24), 3.91 right (35). Both defenses bleed the middle and CAR is tight outside.
matchup.pressure: NE blitz 24%; CAR EPA/dropback vs blitz -0.40 vs +0.04 unblitzed, so pressure should cut Carolina's deep yards and push Young to quick throws. CAR blitz 25%; NE EPA/dropback vs blitz +0.29 vs +0.13 unblitzed, so Maye is not blitz-fragile. NE missing a guard (Wilson Out, Onwenu Q) still raises pressure risk and checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: CAR run defense bleeds: 5.64 YPC and 10 runs of 10-plus in 3 games, plus two linebackers out. NE run defense does not: 3.02 YPC and only 4 runs of 10-plus. NE also allows explosives through the air (20+ pass 14/97) and middle YPA 11.29; CAR has allowed only 6 passes of 20+ (6/99) and chokes the perimeter.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is NE's run game into CAR's bad front and missing linebackers, not a WR1-into-a-weak-corner story (no coverage chart, and McMillan is Q). CAR's primary target (McMillan, 27 targets, 216 yards) would attack NE's explosive/middle leak, but Young-vs-blitz and the calf tag break that overlap. Henry (22 targets) and Stevenson (11 targets, 138 rec yards) are the NE pieces aimed at CAR's middle bleed and vacant linebackers.

pro_edge.script_read: Low total favors unders and a run lean, not volume overs. Spread 5.5 is past 3.5, so the dog (CAR) throws more if trailing and the leader's RB carries rise late. 5.5 is not a blowout flag for automatic starter-snap death, but a two-score lead would still trim NE skill snaps. Own-OL injuries cap how far the run-efficiency edge can be pressed.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Stevenson never became the closer: Henderson, Maye and Gibson split a 24-carry team run game, Wilson's absence and a limited Onwenu held YPC near 3.5, and he finished in the mid-teens the way he did in two of his first three. Carolina's 5.64 YPC was three soft opponents, not a law. Hubbard played, the calf was a decoy, Carolina stayed within a score, and he got his usual 14 carries plus one 30-yard run against a Patriots front that had simply not faced a real run game yet. The 57.5 median was never a soft number, and a game-time active tag turned the under into a fair coin flip.
slip_story: One script only: New England controls a low-total game, runs late into Carolina's leaky front, and Carolina's rushing stalls on a 3.02 YPC defense as the dog falls behind. Stevenson rush over with Hubbard rush under. Do not add Henry, McMillan, Renfrow or Boutte overs; those need pass volume or a shootout. Do not add a total under in the same slip as any receiving over. No touchdown legs, one market per player, max two edges. No stake: no price, and the user's rules are not a bet placement.
